source.title: The Go-Getter
source.author: Peter B. Kyne
source.summary: A short business parable about initiative, persistence, salesmanship, responsibility, and proving reliability under pressure.
source.corePromise: Show how decisive execution and ownership separate serious operators from talkers.

target.positioning: execution, sales, ownership, and operator discipline for founders, technical sellers, creators, and freelancers

us.evidence: Published in 1921 or 1922, before the 1930 U.S. public-domain cutoff active in 2026.

sourceAvailability.location: Public-domain scans and bibliographic records available for editorial source review.

titleConcepts: The Go-Getter in the Age of Startups
subtitleOptions: A Modern Parable About Ownership, Sales, Execution, and Doing the Hard Thing
Peter B. Kyne's Business Classic Rebuilt for Founders, Freelancers, and Operators
adaptation.modernWorld: Startup execution, B2B sales, customer success, technical implementation, founder-led sales, freelancing, operations, and high-trust delivery
toneRules: Make the story energetic, direct, and operational.
Preserve the parable's test of initiative while removing dated workplace assumptions.
Emphasize ownership without glorifying burnout or abusive management.
prohibitedChanges: Do not romanticize exploitation or pointless loyalty tests.
Do not imply Peter B. Kyne wrote the adaptation.
Do not make the test arbitrary; it must reveal useful operating character.
coreLessons: Ownership means solving the real problem, not completing the visible task.
Reliability creates trust faster than self-promotion.
Sales requires courage, follow-up, and useful persistence.
Constraints reveal whether a person thinks or waits.
The best operators protect the mission without losing judgment.

chapterPlan.title: The Assignment Nobody Wants
chapterPlan.focus: Introduce a capable but unproven operator who is given a difficult customer-facing mission.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A technical seller must rescue an enterprise implementation with no clean path.

chapterPlan.title: The Blue Vase Becomes a Production Incident
chapterPlan.focus: Modernize the test into a mission that requires persistence, judgment, and accountability.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A customer deadline, broken vendor chain, and no obvious owner.

chapterPlan.title: No One Is Coming
chapterPlan.focus: Show the protagonist moving from complaint to ownership.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: The operator stops waiting for permission and starts clearing blockers.

chapterPlan.title: Useful Persistence
chapterPlan.focus: Separate smart persistence from harassment, ego, and wasted motion.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Follow-ups, calls, favors, data, and relationship capital.

chapterPlan.title: The Person People Trust
chapterPlan.focus: Show how one hard assignment changes reputation.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: A builder becomes the person customers and leaders call when execution matters.

chapterPlan.title: Ship the Result
chapterPlan.focus: Turn the parable into an operating method.
chapterPlan.modernFrame: Define the real outcome, map constraints, communicate, act, and finish.
